q: Can you give me ___ about universities in the UK?
e: Advice is uncountable: no a/an, no plural.

q: There isn't ___ traffic in the city centre on Sundays.
The teacher gave us too ___ homework.
___ people attended the lecture than we expected.
We bought some new ___ for the living room.
Recent research ___ that sleep improves memory.
e: Research is uncountable, so the verb is singular.

q: I have very ___ time, so I can't help you today.
How ___ (much / many) money do you spend on rent?
How ___ (much / many) students are there in your class?
She gave me two useful ___ of advice.
The news ___ (be) very bad yesterday.
There are only a ___ (few / little) tickets left.
He doesn't have much ___ (experience / experiences) in marketing.
e: Experience as general skill is uncountable.

q: She gave me many informations about the course.
fix: She gave me a lot of information about the course.
e: Information is uncountable: no plural, no 'many'.

q: We need to buy new equipments for the laboratory.
fix: We need to buy new equipment for the laboratory.

q: I have a good news for you.
fix: I have some good news for you.

q: The government should create more works for young people.
fix: The government should create more jobs for young people.
e: Work is uncountable; the countable word is 'job'.

q: Can I ask you an advice?
a: Can I ask you for some advice?
Can I ask you for advice?
Can I ask for some advice?
Can I ask you for a piece of advice?
e: ask (someone) for advice; advice is uncountable.

q: There were less cars on the road today.
a: There were fewer cars on the road today.

q: Recent researches show interesting results.
e: Research is uncountable (singular verb), or use 'studies'.
